Welcome to Northview Primary School where children are at the heart of everything we do.
We are committed to instilling our core values of ambition, responsibility, and excellence within all our pupils.
It is our firm belief that every child deserves the finest opportunities in both life and education, and we are in a unique position to offer these.
Our dedication to providing an inclusive education for all is fundamental to the ethos we uphold at Northview.
It is a privilege to lead an exceptional team, where every member, from our dedicated support staff to our inspiring teachers, prioritises the best interests of our children, delivering a vibrant, creative, and enriching educational experience.
Explore our website to discover more about our school, our values, and the exciting educational journey that awaits your child.

pageCache.text:
Northview Primary School
Together, we can achieve great things!
Our VisionAt Northview Primary School, we aspire to be a nurturing and dynamic learning community where every child is inspired to dream big, act with integrity, and strive for excellence. We believe that primary education lays the foundation for lifelong learning, strong character, and future success. Our vision is to empower every learner to become a confident, compassionate, and capable individual—ready to shape the world of tomorrow.
At our school, we firmly believe that every child can succeed, and it is our mission to ensure that all pupils achieve as best as they can. Central to our ethos is the commitment to an inclusive curriculum that allows each child to flourish, regardless of their individual circumstances or backgrounds. Our ambitious, broad, and balanced curriculum is thoughtfully designed to not only prepare our students for secondary education but also equip them with the skills necessary for life-long success.
We take pride in promoting excellent behaviour, which contributes to a positive learning environment where happy, secure pupils can thrive.
Through an enriched curriculum that incorporates rich cultural experiences, we provide students with opportunities to engage with the world around them, enhancing their understanding and appreciation of diverse perspectives.We believe that together we can make a difference in each child’s educational journey, empowering them to reach their full potential and become confident, capable individuals ready to navigate an increasingly complex world.
AmbitionAt Northview, we foster a culture of high expectations where every child is encouraged to aim high and believe in their own potential. Ambition means nurturing big dreams and setting meaningful goals. It’s about encouraging curiosity, resilience, and the confidence to explore new ideas. We inspire our children to embrace learning as a lifelong journey and to see every challenge as an opportunity to grow.
ResponsibilityWe teach our pupils the importance of responsibility—towards themselves, each other, and the world around them. Responsibility means making thoughtful choices, treating others with kindness and respect, and being active participants in their own learning. At Northview, we help children understand that they have the power to make a positive difference in their community and beyond, by acting with honesty, care, and consideration.
ExcellenceExcellence at Northview is about striving to be the best we can be—in our work, our relationships, and our attitudes. We value perseverance, pride in achievement, and a growth mindset that encourages all learners to overcome obstacles and celebrate progress. We believe that excellence comes from effort, and we support every child to reach their highest potential in a joyful, supportive environment.

Governors
Welcome from the Chair of Governors
As the Chair of Governors, it is a privilege to welcome you to our school community. On behalf of the governing body, I would like to share our vision for Northview and our commitment to every child who walks through our doors.
Our primary role as governors is to provide strategic leadership and ensure that the school delivers the highest quality of education in a safe, nurturing environment. We work closely with the Headteacher and the senior leadership team to set ambitious goals, monitor progress, and ensure that the school’s resources are used effectively to benefit all pupils.
The governing body is made up of volunteers, including parents, staff, and members of the local community. We are all united by a single goal: to see the children of Northview thrive.
We value your feedback and believe that a strong partnership between home and school is the key to success. We look forward to seeing you at school events throughout the year and working together to make Northview Primary the best it can be.
Clive Lawson, Chair of Governors Northview Primary School

Northview Primary School
Together, we can achieve great things!
Music
Our pupils are joyful, confident musicians who listen, perform, create and understand.
Intent
Music is taught by specialist teachers from Brent Music Service, giving pupils a high-quality and progressive musical education from the Early Years to Year 6. We want every child to experience the joy and belonging of making music, develop a confident singing voice and build the musicianship needed to listen, perform, improvise and compose. The Music’sCool pathway progressively develops pulse, rhythm, pitch, notation, instrumental skill, coordination and musical expression, opening pupils’ eyes to music as a lifelong interest and possible future pathway.
Implementation
· In the Early Years, playful singing, movement, listening and percussion establish beat competency, discrimination, coordination, creativity and confidence.
· In Key Stage 1, pupils extend vocal accuracy, rhythm and solfa, read and create simple patterns, handle percussion and begin recorder. In Key Stage 2, learning develops through singing and instrumental work with increasingly secure notation, ensemble skills, improvisation, composition and musical understanding.
· Specialists model high-quality sound, technique and vocabulary. Lessons combine listening, vocal work, movement, practical instrumental learning, rehearsal, creation and performance so that musical knowledge is learned through active music-making.
· Repertoire is chosen to broaden cultural knowledge and musical horizons. Pupils listen with attention, describe expressive and structural features, and learn how music is shaped by context and purpose.
· Scaffolds, adapted parts, visual notation, repeated modelling and ensemble roles enable all pupils to contribute. School performances, choir and links with Brent Music Service provide authentic audiences and enrichment.
Impact
Pupils sing and play with growing accuracy, fluency, control and expression. They maintain a part, follow and use notation at an age-appropriate level, listen analytically, improvise and compose, and evaluate performances using musical vocabulary. Specialist assessment, classroom observation, recordings and performances show progression and participation. Pupils leave with musical confidence, positive memories and a foundation for further study.
Our values in action
Pupils encounter expert teaching, challenging repertoire and inspiring performance opportunities.
They rehearse reliably, listen to others and contribute to the success of an ensemble.
They refine technique, attend to musical detail and perform with commitment and expression.

Art and Design
Pupils are confident artists who explore, create, reflect and develop a distinctive visual voice.
Intent
Art and Design at Northview gives every pupil the knowledge, skill and confidence to communicate ideas visually. Using Kapow Primary’s condensed curriculum, pupils develop practical, theoretical and disciplinary knowledge: they learn how to make art, learn about artists and creative traditions, and learn how to evaluate and analyse. We want pupils to experiment courageously, appreciate art from a wide range of cultures and periods, and understand that ideas develop through observation, practice, reflection and refinement.
Implementation
Impact
Pupils use a growing repertoire of materials, techniques and formal elements with increasing control and purpose. They draw on knowledge of artists, generate and develop ideas, explain their choices, respond constructively to feedback and refine work. Progress is visible in sketchbooks, final outcomes and pupil commentary. Review focuses on the development of knowledge and artistic decision-making over time, not on a single preferred style or uniform product.
Our values in action
Pupils take creative risks, study significant art and pursue increasingly sophisticated ideas.
They use materials safely and sustainably, care for shared resources and critique respectfully.
They practise techniques, attend to detail and improve work through reflection and refinement.
Art and Design Overview

Northview Primary School
Together, we can achieve great things!
Computing
We aim to develop safe, creative and computational thinkers who use technology confidently and purposefully.
Intent
Computing at Northview is delivered by Junior Jam specialists through a progressive curriculum from Reception to Year 6. We want pupils not only to use technology effectively for learning, but also to understand and navigate the technology they encounter beyond school. The curriculum combines computing with engaging digital media, including animation and music production, so pupils discover new interests and possible future pathways. Across computer science, information technology and digital literacy, pupils develop the knowledge, confidence and judgement to create, communicate, solve problems and participate safely in an increasingly digital world.
Implementation
Impact
Pupils use technology with increasing confidence, independence and purpose. They can explain and apply age-appropriate programming concepts, select suitable digital tools, create and refine digital content, solve problems computationally and communicate using accurate vocabulary. Crucially, they recognise online risks, know how to respond and make responsible choices. Progress is evidenced through digital outcomes, practical observation, pupil explanation, knowledge checks and Junior Jam’s ongoing assessment information.
Our values in action
Pupils create with a wide range of technologies and see themselves as future digital innovators.
They protect privacy, behave respectfully online, evaluate risk and use technology ethically.
They debug, refine and evaluate digital work, using precise vocabulary and efficient solutions.
Northview Primary School

Northview Primary School
Together, we can achieve great things!
Design Technology
Our pupils are resourceful designers who identify needs, create purposeful products and improve them.
Intent
Design and Technology enables pupils to turn ideas into purposeful, well-considered products. Through Kapow Primary’s condensed curriculum, pupils learn to identify needs, research users and existing products, create clear design criteria, make accurately and evaluate honestly. The curriculum combines creativity with technical knowledge and practical skill, helping pupils become resourceful problem-solvers who understand that effective design improves through testing, feedback and iteration.
Implementation
· Progressive projects develop the recurring design process: research and generate ideas; communicate and plan; make; test; evaluate; and improve.
· Across Reception to Year 6, pupils build knowledge and skill through structures, mechanisms and mechanical systems, textiles, cooking and nutrition, electrical systems and the digital world, as age appropriate.
· Knowledge organisers establish key vocabulary, prior learning and technical concepts. Teachers explicitly model safe and accurate use of tools, materials, components and joining or finishing techniques.
· Projects have a clear purpose, intended user and design criteria. Pupils explore existing products and designers, make annotated plans or prototypes, select resources for their properties and explain their decisions.
· Cooking develops practical food preparation alongside knowledge of nutrition, hygiene and where food comes from. Sustainability and responsible material choices are discussed where relevant.
· Testing is integral: pupils compare products against criteria and user needs, identify improvements and refine rather than treating the first outcome as final.
Impact
Pupils become increasingly independent and technically capable designers. They can define a problem, generate and communicate ideas, choose appropriate materials and tools, make safely and accurately, and evaluate a product against clear criteria. Books, prototypes, finished products, photographs and pupil explanations show progression. Leaders review whether pupils can transfer technical knowledge between projects and whether all groups take an active role in designing and making.
Our values in action
Pupils tackle authentic design problems and develop original, purposeful solutions.
They design for users, work safely, reduce waste and consider the wider impact of choices.
They value accuracy, functionality, quality of finish and iterative improvement.
Design Technology Overview

Northview Primary School
Together, we can achieve great things!
At Northview, we recognise the importance of embedding early reading to ensure our children have every opportunity to access the whole curriculum. Our phonics provision aims to ensure that all pupils can read easily, fluently and with good understanding. It allows pupils to apply their phonics decoding skills to read and comprehend text as well as write and compose sentences.
At Northview we use Read Write Inc Phonics (RWI) to give your child the best possible start with their literacy. We have put together a guide to how the RWI programme works together with some useful links.
What is Read Write Inc?
Read Write Inc (RWI) is a phonics validated programme which helps all children learn to read fluently and at speed so they can focus on developing their skills in comprehension, vocabulary and spelling. The programme is designed for children aged 4-7. However, at Northview we begin the programme in Nursery and will continue teaching RWI to children beyond the age of 7 if they still need support in their reading.
RWI was developed by Ruth Miskin and more information on this can be found here.
Five key principles underpin the teaching in all Read Write Inc. sessions
Purpose – know the purpose of every activity and share it with the children, so they know the one thing they should be thinking about
Participation – ensure every child participates throughout the lesson. Partnership work is fundamental to learning
Praise – ensure children are praised for effort and learning, not ability
Pace – teach at an effective pace and devote every moment to teaching and learning
Passion – be passionate about teaching so children can be engaged emotionally.
When appropriate, children are introduced to the initial sounds in short, normally 10-15 minutes sessions.
In Reception all children learn how to ‘read’ the sounds in words and how those sounds can be written down.

Children follow the same format as Reception but will work on complex sounds and read books appropriate to their reading level . Daily sessions of RWI phonics last for 45 minutes.
Children are taught the sounds in 3 sets
Set 1 Sounds are taught in the following order together with rhymes to help children form the letters correctly and instantly recognise sounds ready for blending.

***We do not use letter names at this early stage.
We use pure sounds (‘m’ not’ muh’,’s’ not ‘suh’, etc.) so that the child is be able to blend the sounds into words more easily.
At Northview we use a puppet called Fred who is an expert on sounding out words! we call it, ‘Fred Talk’.

Children will also use pictures for each sound to help recognise the sound and then form the shape of the sound.
The children are then taught Set 2 Sounds - the long vowels. When they are very confident with all of set 1 and 2 they are taught Set 3 Sounds.

Nonsense words (Alien words)
As well as learning to read and blend real words, children will have plenty of opportunities to apply their sound recognition skills on reading ‘Nonsense words’. These words will also feature heavily in the Year One Phonics Screening check in the summer term.
Children will be introduced to ‘Ditty books’ when they successfully begin to read single words. Children use sound-blending (Fred Talk) to read short ditties. They will bring these home once they have read and discussed the book in class. Children will then be challenged to use their developing phonic knowledge to write short sentences.
Within all the books children will have Red and Green words to learn in order to help them to become speedy readers.
Red words are words that are not easily decodable and challenge words to extend children’s vocabulary.
Green words are linked to the sounds they have been learning and are easily decodable.
Dots and dashes represent the sound each letter makes. Once your child has been introduced and taught these words in school we will send them home for you to continue practising with your child.
During the RWI session children will read the book three times and at each new reading they will have plenty of opportunities to practise using their developing comprehension skills. You may have heard your child talking about ‘hold, edit or build a sentence’.
Hold a sentence is an activity that encourages children to remember a whole sentence while focusing on spelling and punctuation.
Build a sentence is to give children the opportunity to create their own sentence that makes sense.
Edit a sentence allows the children to check their sentence and make the necessary changes using their knowledge of spelling punctuation and grammar.
Finally, children complete a longer piece of independent writing, which gives them the opportunity to implement their phonics knowledge to practice their spelling, grammar and punctuation.
A spelling quiz is held each week (this will only start in Reception when children are ready to write and form their letters). Children are encouraged to use ‘Fred fingers’ to first sound out a word before they write it down. Children learn how to spell rather than just get tested. Furthermore, this way of teaching spellings allows children to use Fred fingers whenever they get stuck with spelling a word. Children pinch each sound on fingers before writing the word.
Order of Story books
